topic: First-time home buyer, 2025: FHSA ($8,000/yr, $40,000 lifetime, deductible in, tax-free qualifying withdrawal), Home Buyers' Plan (up to $60,000 from RRSPs, was $35,000; repay over 15 years, start deferred to the 5th year after the withdrawal year for first withdrawals 2022–2025), both usable for the same home; home buyers' amount $10,000 (line 31270) × 14.5% = $1,450 federal

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Jamie, first home bought in 2025; FHSA opened 2023, $8,000 contributed in each of 2023, 2024, 2025 = $24,000 (growth ignored); HBP withdrawal $35,000 in 2025 (limit $60,000); $24,000 + $35,000 = $59,000; HBTC $10,000 × 14.5% = $1,450 federal; HBP repayment 1/15 a year = $2,333.33 starting 2030 (5th year after 2025).

spoken_manual.credit: fourteen hundred and fifty = $1,450 = $10,000 × 14.5% (checked by hand)
spoken_manual.repay_start: 'starting in twenty thirty' = 5th year after the 2025 withdrawal year
spoken_manual.hbp_old_screen: former $35,000 limit shown on screen only (not spoken)

sources.fhsa: canada.ca CRA 'Make the most of your first home savings account' (tax tips 2025) and CRA FHSA page: annual limit $8,000, lifetime $40,000, carry-forward up to $8,000
sources.hbp: canada.ca CRA housing tax tips 2025: enhanced HBP, withdraw up to $60,000 (Budget 2024 raised it from $35,000); CRA HBP page: repayment starts in the 5th year after the withdrawal year for first withdrawals 2022-01-01 to 2025-12-31 (temporary relief)
sources.both: canada.ca CRA: HBP withdrawal and FHSA qualifying withdrawal can be used for the same qualifying home if all conditions are met at each withdrawal
sources.hbtc: canada.ca CRA line 31270 Home buyers' amount: up to $10,000 for a qualifying home bought in 2025; non-refundable; 2025 federal rate 14.5% (5013 Schedule B)
